newsitem.title: MEXICO: FORECAST-Telmex Q3 seen showing recovery.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Telmex Q3 seen showing recovery.

text.p: Mexican telephone giant Telefonos de Mexico SA (Telmex) is expected to report third quarter earnings this week that show a slow recovery from Mexico's recession.
A survey of seven industry analysts forecast third quarter earnings per share of $1.01 per ADR.
Analysts said line growth for the telephone giant -- the best measure of revenue -- would remain an anemic 1.9 percent year-on-year.
Despite poor line growth, tariff increases earlier this year and a slight increase in volume should provide healthy revenue growth compared with the year-ago quarter, analysts said.

"Although a recovery in line demand is not yet apparent, we believe that the compound effect of the local and long distance tariffs implemented throughout 1996 will boost results," Santander Investment said in a report.
Other analysts said discount programs begun by Telmex this quarter should keep revenues fairly flat compared with the second quarter.
Discount programs have cut prices for some business and retail customers in an effort to protect market share ahead of competition in 1997.
"The key variable is to what degree is the reduction in prices going to increase volumes?" said Paul Aran, a telecommunications analyst at James Capel.
Although the discount programs may have hurt revenues slightly, analysts praised Telmex for pre-emptively fighting to protect market share ahead of next year.

"They are being very aggressive in trying to maintain market share," said Shayne McGuire, an analyst at Deutche Morgan Grenfell. He said long-distance margins could fall slightly as a result of the discount programs.
Analysts were divided as to whether or not operating margin would rise or fall from the 36 percent during the second quarter.

They also said non-cash financial items such as foreign exchange gains or losses could also vary widely. Some forecast financial gains of about 400 million pesos during the quarter, largely due to a stronger peso.
Some analysts said that this quarter will not give a clear idea of how well Telmex will be able to handle the competition next year -- when it loses its historic monopoly.
"No matter what the third quarter turns out like, people will still be looking at competition kicking in within a quarter," said Simon Flannery, an analyst at JP Morgan.

He said he would look closely at long-distance revenues to see if Telmex and its rivals will have a bigger pie to divide between them. "Up to now, we haven't seen much evidence of a recovery in the economy feeding through to the telecommunications market," he said.
